A Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID) is an identifier included in all wireless packets; it is not given to monitored devices.
A blackout period is a time administrators set when alerts are suspended, not a per-device assignment.

questions.stem: Which basic function of a Network Monitoring System (NMS) visualizes the network to aid and speed troubleshooting?

questions.reviewCue: Like an aerial photo of a parking lot that shows at once where every car sits.

questions.stem: A system that checks a network for problems caused by overloaded or crashed servers has five basic functions. Which one keeps an eye on the network?

keywords.text: keeps an eye on the network

answers.rationale: Discover finds the devices on the network and how they are connected, before any watching starts.
Monitor keeps an eye on the network and provides a large selection of monitors.
Map visualizes the network; it is the picture, not the watch.
Alert notifies network administrators when something goes wrong; it is not the function that keeps watch.

questions.stem: As a starting point, which item is one of the "big 5" that network administrators want to check?

answers.rationale: Switch fans are other hardware components that most tools also cover beyond the big 5.
Power supplies in a switch are other hardware that most tools also cover beyond the big 5.
Disk is one of the big 5, with ping availability and latency, Central Processing Unit (CPU), memory and interface utilization.
Network route analytics is another statistic Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) obtain; it is not one of the big 5.

questions.reviewCue: Like the short list of vital signs a medic checks first before running any deeper tests.

questions.stem: Which basic function of a Network Monitoring System (NMS) notifies network administrators when something goes wrong?

answers.rationale: Alert is the function in which Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) notify network administrators when something goes wrong.
Map visualizes the network; it sends no notices.

questions.reviewCue: Think of the moment a quiet watch turns into a tap on the shoulder: something needs you now.

answers.rationale: Discover finds the devices on the network and how they are connected; it keeps no history.
Report deals with real-time and historical reporting; Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) provide real-time and historical monitoring data.

questions.stem: What are the webpages called in which a Network Monitoring System (NMS) delivers monitoring information?

answers.rationale: A Management Information Base (MIB) maintains the objects that Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) queries; it is not a webpage.
Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) deliver monitoring information in webpages called dashboards, which are made up of turn-key views.
Monitoring templates, kept in a Network Monitoring System (NMS) library, define how to monitor a device; they are not webpages.

questions.reviewCue: Like the front page of a news site, pulling the most important headlines onto one screen.

questions.stem: What aims to catch hackers before they do real damage to a network?

answers.rationale: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) aims to catch hackers before they do real damage to a network.
A Management Information Base (MIB) defines all the information a managed device exposes; it catches no hackers.

answers.text: A Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agent
answers.rationale: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) software agents respond to status requests from the Network Monitoring System (NMS); they do not hunt for attackers.
Syslog automatically sends messages when an event affects a network device; it does not hunt hackers.

questions.reviewCue: Like a lifeguard who steps in before a struggling swimmer gets hurt.

questions.stem: How does an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) work?

answers.text: By querying objects maintained in a Management Information Base (MIB)
answers.rationale: Querying objects kept in a Management Information Base (MIB) is how Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) collects data, not how an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) spots attacks.

answers.text: By suspending alerts during blackout periods that administrators configure
answers.rationale: Blackout periods are times some Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) suspend alerts, such as when printers are shut down.

answers.text: By looking for signatures of known attacks or deviations from normal activity
answers.rationale: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) work by looking for signatures of known attacks or deviations from normal activity.

answers.text: By establishing variables in agents and recognizing asynchronous events
answers.rationale: Establishing variables in agents and recognizing asynchronous events are Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) management tool functions.

questions.reviewCue: Think of a fingerprint file kept at a police station, and a neighbor who knows the street's usual rhythm.

questions.stem: Which statistic that a Network Monitoring System (NMS) obtains tells whether a server is up and responding to requests?

answers.rationale: Network response time asks how fast each request is processed, not whether anything is up.
Memory utilization is a performance metric that fluctuates during the day; it is not the up-and-responding check.

questions.reviewCue: Like calling a shop to see whether anyone picks up the phone before you drive over.

questions.stem: Which statistic that a Network Monitoring System (NMS) obtains tells how fast each request is processed?

keywords.text: how fast each request is processed

answers.rationale: Service or device availability asks whether the service or device is up and responding at all.
Central Processing Unit (CPU) utilization is a performance metric that fluctuates during the day, not a per-request speed.
Network response time asks how fast each request is processed.

questions.reviewCue: Like clocking how long a cashier takes to ring up each customer in line.

questions.stem: Which statistic that a Network Monitoring System (NMS) obtains shows the paths and hops that requests travel between client and server, and whether those paths are optimal?

answers.rationale: Network route analytics asks which routes and hops requests travel through and whether routes are optimal.
Network response time asks how fast each request is processed, not which way it travels.
Interface utilization is a performance metric that fluctuates during the day; it traces no paths.

questions.reviewCue: Like a trip planner checking each stop between home and work and whether a faster option exists.

questions.stem: In many Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs), which basic function requires a significant amount of manual processing?

answers.rationale: Monitor keeps an eye on the network; it is not where many Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) need manual processing.
Many Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) require a significant amount of manual processing to create a network map.
Alert is where Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) notify network administrators when something goes wrong.

questions.reviewCue: Like assembling a jigsaw puzzle by hand because the box came with no picture on its lid.

questions.stem: Some Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) merely provide a drawing tool and rely on the network administrator's knowledge for which basic function?

answers.rationale: Some Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) merely provide a drawing tool and rely on the administrator's knowledge to map out the network.
Monitor keeps an eye on the network; it uses no drawing tool.
Alert is where Network Monitoring Systems (NMSs) notify network administrators when something goes wrong; it uses no drawing tool.

questions.reviewCue: Like being handed a blank sketchpad and asked to sketch your neighborhood from memory.

questions.stem: Physical and logical network diagrams are a good reference source when carrying out which basic function of a Network Monitoring System (NMS)?

answers.rationale: Discover finds the devices on the network and how they are connected; the diagrams are not named as its reference.
Monitor keeps an eye on the network; the diagrams are not named as its reference.
Report deals with real-time and historical reporting; the diagrams are not named as its reference.
Physical and logical network diagrams are a good reference source for developing network maps.

questions.reviewCue: Like consulting a recipe card you wrote earlier when teaching a friend to cook the same dish.

questions.stem: A system that checks a network for problems caused by overloaded or crashed servers has five basic functions. In most tools, which one also covers the fans and power supplies in a switch?

keywords.text: fans and power supplies in a switch

answers.rationale: Most network monitoring tools provide monitors for hardware such as switch fans and power supplies.
Discover finds the devices on the network and how they are connected; it checks no fans.
Map visualizes the network; it checks no hardware components.
Alert notifies network administrators when something goes wrong; the hardware checks belong elsewhere.

questions.reviewCue: Like a mechanic's inspection that checks the oil level and engine heat, not just the tire pressure.

questions.stem: Which basic function of a Network Monitoring System (NMS) is configured with a time element so that brief threshold blips during peak usage do not bother administrators?

answers.rationale: Discover finds the devices on the network and how they are connected; it has no time element.
Map visualizes the network; it has no time element.
Network Monitoring System (NMS) alerts are configured with a time element, so an alert is issued only when a threshold stays exceeded.
Monitor keeps an eye on the network; the time element is set on a different function.

questions.reviewCue: Like shrugging off one sneeze but calling the doctor when a cough lasts for days.

questions.stem: An airman finds data errors on a signal cable. A meter shows the cable's voltage rising and falling continuously for as long as a nearby motor runs, and the readings settle when the motor stops. No storm, static spark or sudden release of stored charge is involved. MSgt Rush asks the airman to name this disturbance. Which term is best supported?

keywords.text: rising and falling continuously for as long as a nearby motor runs

answers.text: Transient voltage coming from the running motor
answers.rationale: Transient voltage is a brief surge, usually from components suddenly releasing stored electricity or from lightning, not a fluctuation lasting the whole run.

answers.text: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) coming from the running motor
answers.rationale: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) is a disruption that produces fluctuations in voltage or current, and this one lasts while the motor runs.

answers.text: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) coming from the running motor
answers.rationale: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) is the sudden flow of electricity between two charged objects, and no static spark is involved here.

answers.text: Triboelectricity coming from the running motor
answers.rationale: Triboelectricity is the charge developed by friction, static electricity at rest, not a fluctuation on a cable.

questions.stem: In a communications facility, the readings on the data circuits between two equipment racks keep shifting up and down whenever nearby equipment starts. The racks and their circuits are otherwise working. MSgt Rush asks an airman which grounding measure is designed to keep this kind of disturbance under control. Which measure is best supported?

keywords.text: keep shifting up and down whenever nearby equipment starts

answers.text: The earth electrode subsystem of the facility ground system
answers.rationale: The earth electrode subsystem provides the connection between the earth and the other facility ground subsystems, not a voltage reference for circuits.

answers.text: The equipment fault protective subsystem of the facility ground system
answers.rationale: The equipment fault protective subsystem protects personnel and equipment from voltages caused by faults in electrical circuits, and no fault is described.

answers.text: Workstation and personnel grounding, an Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) control measure
answers.rationale: Workstation and personnel grounding is one of the three Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) control measures, not a facility ground subsystem.

answers.text: The signal reference subsystem of the facility ground system
answers.rationale: Voltage fluctuations are Electromagnetic Interference (EMI), and the signal reference subsystem controls electrical noise and static in a facility.

questions.stem: Two metal equipment cabinets stand side by side, and a test shows that the joint between them strongly resists electricity passing from one cabinet to the other. MSgt Rush tells an airman to cut that resistance at the joint before the cabinets go into service. Which practice is best supported for this task?

keywords.text: strongly resists electricity passing from one cabinet to the other

answers.text: Bond the two cabinets to each other across the joint
answers.rationale: Impedance is the opposition electricity faces, and bonding establishes a low-impedance path between two metal surfaces such as these cabinets.

answers.text: Ground the two cabinets to each other across the joint
answers.rationale: Grounding is a conductive path between the earth and a grounded object, not a low-impedance path from one cabinet to the other.

answers.text: Tie the two cabinets to each other through the earth electrode subsystem
answers.rationale: The earth electrode subsystem connects the earth to the other facility ground subsystems, not one cabinet directly to the other.

answers.text: Cover the joint with protective packaging that controls resistance
answers.rationale: Packaging resistance is controlled to minimize the buildup and discharge of static, not to lower opposition at a metal joint.

questions.stem: A base project will install fiber optic cabling throughout a new office building. The work uses ordinary commercial products and installation practices, and nothing in it was designed or reworked for the armed services. MSgt Rush asks an airman which publication the installers should follow for the cabling. Which publication is best supported?

keywords.text: ordinary commercial products and installation practices

answers.text: Military Standard (MIL-STD) 1678 Fiber Optic Cabling Systems Requirements and Measurements
answers.rationale: A Military Standard (MIL-STD) sets requirements for military-unique or substantially modified commercial processes, and this job uses ordinary commercial practices.
Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) 568-C.4 is the Broadband Coaxial Cabling and Components Standard, which covers coaxial cabling rather than fiber.
Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) 568-C.3 is the Optical Fiber Cabling and Components Standard, and Military Standards (MIL-STDs) target military-unique processes.
Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) 942-A is the Telecommunications Infrastructure Standard for Data Centers, not the fiber cabling and components standard.

questions.stem: An airman has an old copy of an Air Force Instruction (AFI) on cyber incident handling saved on a desktop computer. Before work starts, MSgt Rush wants the airman to download the current version and to know which publication series to search for it. Which plan is best supported?

keywords.text: an old copy of an Air Force Instruction (AFI) on cyber incident handling

answers.text: Download the 91-series Air Force Instruction (AFI) from the E-Pubs website
answers.rationale: All Air Force publications covering safety are in the 91-series, while cyber-related Air Force Instructions (AFIs) start with a 17.

answers.text: Download the 91-series Air Force Instruction (AFI) from the Executive Services Directorate website
answers.rationale: The Executive Services Directorate website is where a downloaded Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) is verified, and safety publications are 91-series.

answers.text: Download the 17-series Air Force Instruction (AFI) from the Executive Services Directorate website
answers.rationale: The Executive Services Directorate website is where a downloaded Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) is verified, not an Air Force Instruction (AFI).

answers.text: Download the 17-series Air Force Instruction (AFI) from the E-Pubs website
answers.rationale: Cyber-related Air Force Instructions (AFIs) start with a 17, and a downloaded AFI is verified as current against the E-Pubs website.

questions.stem: In a squadron communications closet, one device takes each piece of data arriving from the office computers, reads its destination Media Access Control (MAC) address and sends it out only toward the computer that holds that address. MSgt Rush asks an airman to identify the device and the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer it operates at. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: reads its destination Media Access Control (MAC) address

answers.text: The closet's switch, operating at Layer 2
answers.rationale: Media Access Control (MAC) addresses are added in the Layer 2 header of the Data Link Layer (DLL), and switches are the devices that operate at Layer 2.

answers.text: The closet's router, operating at Layer 3
answers.rationale: Routers operate at Layer 3 and connect networks, but Media Access Control (MAC) addresses are added in the Layer 2 header.

answers.text: The closet's router, operating at Layer 2
answers.rationale: Routers operate at Layer 3, the Network layer, and connect networks such as a private network to the internet; they are not Layer 2 devices.

answers.text: The closet's switch, operating at Layer 3
answers.rationale: Layer 3 is the Network layer, where routers operate; switches operate at Layer 2, the Data Link Layer (DLL).

questions.stem: Traffic between two base networks keeps taking a slow, roundabout route even though a more direct one exists. MSgt Rush suspects the device that decides how traffic gets from one network to the other. An airman must say which Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer that device works at and whether that layer is one of the upper or lower layers. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: decides how traffic gets from one network to the other

answers.rationale: Layers 5-7 are the upper layers, which contain application-level data, so Layer 3, where routers operate, is not one of them.
Layer 2 is where switches operate, connecting computers, printers and servers to the private network; routers operate at Layer 3.
Layer 2 is where switches operate, and Layers 5-7 are the upper layers, so Layer 2 is not one of them.
Routers choose the best path for information and operate at Layer 3, and Layers 1-4 are the lower layers, which mostly move data around.

questions.stem: Files sent to a base office arrive intact and their plain text reads normally, but the Graphics Interchange Format (GIF) and Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) pictures inside them will not display on any computer. MSgt Rush asks an airman to name the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer whose standards cover those picture formats and whether it is an upper or lower layer. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: pictures inside them will not display

answers.rationale: Graphics Interchange Format (GIF) and Joint Photographic Experts Group (JPEG) are Layer 6 standards, and Layers 5-7 are the upper layers.
Layers 1-4 are the lower layers, mostly concerned with moving data around, so Layer 6 is not one of them.
Layer 4 protocols are Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not picture formats, and Layers 1-4 are the lower layers.
Layer 4 is the Transport layer, whose protocols are Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not picture format standards.

questions.stem: An airman monitors a Web browser session between a base computer and a Web server. The Web server answers on its own service port, while the base computer's side of the session uses a port numbered 49152 or higher, up to 65535. MSgt Rush asks the airman what is true of the base computer's port. Which choice is best supported?

keywords.text: a port numbered 49152 or higher, up to 65535

answers.text: It is a registered port the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) gave the browser
answers.rationale: Registered or user ports range from 1024 to 49151, so a port numbered 49152 or higher is not a registered port.

answers.text: It is a dynamic port assigned for this session and released afterward
answers.rationale: Ports 49152-65535 are the dynamic, private or ephemeral ports, which are assigned as needed and released when the service is finished.

answers.text: It is a well-known port reserved for Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP)
It is a dynamic port kept and reused for later sessions
answers.rationale: Dynamic ports are released when the service is finished, so a service might have a different port assigned every time it is used.

questions.stem: A custom application service is being set up on base, and an airman wants the service to have an officially assigned port number. The airman plans to ask the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) for a port numbered between 49152 and 65535 for the service. MSgt Rush must decide whether IANA would make that assignment. Which choice is best supported?

answers.text: Yes: it assigns whatever port number an application service requests
answers.rationale: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) assigns registered ports, which range from 1024 to 49151, for specific application services.

answers.text: Yes: it would make that port a well-known port for the service
No: it assigns well-known ports but not registered ones
answers.rationale: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) also assigns registered ports from 1024 to 49151 to the requesting entity for specific application services.

answers.text: No: that range lies outside the registered ports it assigns
answers.rationale: The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) assigns registered ports for application services, and ports 49152-65535 lie outside the registered ports.

questions.stem: A new laptop joins a base network and must receive its Internet Protocol (IP) address automatically, without an airman typing one in. MSgt Rush asks the airman to name both the protocol that supplies the address and the transport protocol that carries that protocol's messages. Which pairing is best supported?

keywords.text: receive its Internet Protocol (IP) address automatically

answers.text: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), not User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
answers.rationale: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) is a connectionless protocol, while Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) guarantees packets arrive in the order sent.

answers.text: Domain Name System (DNS) over User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
Domain Name System (DNS) over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), not User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) over User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
answers.rationale: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) automatically assigns dynamic addresses and is connectionless, and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), unlike Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), is connectionless.

questions.stem: A base mail server must hand outgoing mail, with files attached, to the mail server at another base. An airman setting up the firewall rules must know which protocol moves the mail between the two servers and which transport protocol that protocol relies on. MSgt Rush asks the airman for both. Which pairing is best supported?

keywords.text: hand outgoing mail, with files attached

answers.text: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) over User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
answers.rationale: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) permits remote monitoring and management of devices and hosts; it does not transfer mail.

answers.text: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), not User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
answers.rationale: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) transfers email messages and attachments and requires the reliable ordered delivery that Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides.

answers.text: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) over User Datagram Protocol (UDP), not Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
answers.rationale: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) requires the reliable ordered delivery that Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides, not User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

answers.text: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) over Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), not User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
answers.rationale: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is a connectionless protocol for remote monitoring and management of devices; it does not transfer mail.

questions.stem: Two routers on a base network exchange routing information using the Routing Information Protocol (RIP). An airman reviewing the design asks whether each router must first set up a session with its neighbor and confirm it before any routing update is sent. MSgt Rush must answer the airman. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: first set up a session with its neighbor

answers.text: No: it sends updates over User Datagram Protocol (UDP) with no prior arrangement
answers.rationale: Routing Information Protocol (RIP) uses broadcast User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packets, and UDP is connectionless, sending data without prior arrangement.

answers.text: Yes: it sets up a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection with each neighbor
answers.rationale: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) guarantees ordered delivery, but Routing Information Protocol (RIP) uses broadcast User Datagram Protocol (UDP) data packets.

answers.text: Yes: User Datagram Protocol (UDP) re-sends each update that its neighbor does not receive
answers.rationale: Re-sending data the destination does not receive is connection-oriented delivery, while User Datagram Protocol (UDP), which Routing Information Protocol (RIP) uses, is connectionless.

answers.text: No: it sends updates through Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) instead
answers.rationale: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) converts an Internet Protocol (IP) address into a Media Access Control (MAC) address; it does not carry routing updates.

questions.stem: An airman copies a large file between two base computers using the File Transfer Protocol (FTP). Partway through the transfer, one segment of the file does not reach the receiving computer. MSgt Rush asks the airman what happens to that missing segment. Which outcome is best supported?

keywords.text: one segment of the file does not reach the receiving computer

answers.text: It is lost, because the transfer uses connectionless User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
answers.rationale: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) requires the reliable ordered delivery that Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides, not User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

answers.text: It is lost, because the network gives no guarantee of delivery
answers.rationale: Connectionless communication gives no delivery guarantee, but File Transfer Protocol (FTP) requires Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) delivery.

answers.text: It is sent again, because the transfer uses connection-oriented Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
answers.rationale: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) requires Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) delivery, and connection-oriented delivery re-sends any data the destination does not receive.

answers.text: It is skipped, and the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Urgent Pointer field marks the gap
answers.rationale: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Urgent Pointer field is used primarily for out-of-band data that needs special priority, not for marking lost segments.

questions.stem: An airman reviewing an Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) address written in binary sees that the first octet begins with the bits 110. Before the airman records the address in a network plan, MSgt Rush asks what the class of this address is meant for. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: the first octet begins with the bits 110

answers.rationale: A zero in the first bit identifies Class A, used for large networks, so an address beginning with 110 is not Class A.
The first two bits 10 identify Class B, used for intermediate-sized networks, so an address beginning with 110 is not Class B.
Class D is reserved for multicast (designated recipients) addressing, while the first three bits 110 identify Class C, the class used for small networks.
The leading bits 110 identify the Class C address class, and Class C addresses are used for small networks.

questions.stem: An airman is typing an Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) address into an equipment record by hand, and the record form rejects any symbol that cannot appear in such an address. MSgt Rush asks how many different symbols the form must accept for each digit position of the address. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: how many different symbols the form must accept for each digit position

answers.rationale: Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) addresses are written in hexadecimal, which uses the ten digits 0 through 9 followed by the six letters A through F.
Ten symbols, the digits 0 through 9, make up the decimal system, which Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) text representations use instead.
Two symbols, the digits 0 and 1, make up the binary system, not the hexadecimal text an Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6) address is written in.
Four is the number of binary digits that represent one hexadecimal digit, not the number of symbols one hexadecimal digit can use.

questions.stem: An airman is building a training aid that labels the network part and the host part of several Internet Protocol Version 4 (IPv4) addresses. MSgt Rush hands over 225.2.3.40 as the next address on the list. Which part of this address should the airman label as its host number?

answers.text: 40, the last octet of the address
answers.rationale: The last eight bits (1 octet) identify the node number of a Class C address, but 225 falls in the Class D range of 224-239.

answers.text: No octet, since the address is a Class C address
answers.rationale: A Class C address uses its last eight bits (1 octet) for the node number, and 225 falls in the Class D range of 224-239.

answers.text: No octet, since the address has no host field
answers.rationale: The number 225 falls in the Class D range of 224-239, reserved for multicast, a membership addressing function that has no host field.

answers.text: 2.3.40, the last three octets of the address
answers.rationale: The last 24 bits (3 octets) identify the host number of a Class A address, but 225 falls in the Class D range of 224-239.

questions.stem: An installation must link the networks in several of its buildings, which sit miles apart, and no cable can run between the buildings. The plan also rules out any equipment that needs a service provider account to work. MSgt Rush asks an airman which wireless network type fits this plan. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: several of its buildings, which sit miles apart
rules out any equipment that needs a service provider account to work

answers.rationale: A Wireless Metropolitan Area Network (WMAN) is intended to cover around 31 miles (50 kilometers), reaching the distant buildings, while provider subscription is a Wireless Wide Area Network (WWAN) requirement.
A Wireless Wide Area Network (WWAN) covers a wide area, but its handheld devices must be provisioned (subscribed) to a service provider's network, which the plan rules out.
A Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) links devices within a limited area such as a home, school or office building, not buildings miles apart.
A Wireless Personal Area Network (WPAN) uses a technology that enables wireless communication within a range of about 10 meters, far short of miles.

questions.stem: The network administrators installed two Access Points (APs) on one floor of a squadron building. An airman checks two laptops in different rooms on that floor: both show the same network name as the installed access points, but each laptop reports a different Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID). MSgt Rush asks what this shows about the laptops' connections. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: both show the same network name
each laptop reports a different Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID)

answers.text: Each laptop has joined a different Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN)
answers.rationale: The shared name is the Service Set Identifier (SSID), the identifier that tells devices which network to join, so both laptops joined one Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN).

answers.text: The laptops use separate Access Points (APs) on one network
answers.rationale: The shared Service Set Identifier (SSID) names one Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN), and each Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID) is the Media Access Control (MAC) address of a different Access Point (AP), so each laptop uses its own AP.

answers.text: Both laptops are inside the Basic Service Set (BSS) of one Access Point (AP)
answers.rationale: Each Access Point (AP) has its own Basic Service Set (BSS), and its Media Access Control (MAC) address is the ID of that BSS, so two Basic Service Set Identifiers (BSSIDs) mean two APs.

answers.text: One of the laptops has formed a Wireless Ad Hoc Network
answers.rationale: An ad hoc network does not rely on a central Access Point (AP), yet both laptops show the network name of the installed access points.

questions.stem: A squadron's maintainers look up job steps on handheld devices while they walk between aircraft all shift. In the same squadron, one imagery workstation moves large files across the local network all day. MSgt Rush asks an airman to choose a connection type for the maintainers and one for the imagery workstation. Which answer is best supported?

keywords.text: moves large files across the local network all day

answers.text: Wired for the maintainers and wired for the imagery workstation
answers.rationale: Wireless gives increased mobility and roaming without losing the connection, which maintainers walking between aircraft need.

answers.text: Wireless for the maintainers and wireless for the imagery workstation
answers.rationale: Wireless is significantly slower than wired when transferring files over a Local Area Network (LAN), so the imagery workstation's large files belong on a wired link.

answers.text: Wired for the maintainers and wireless for the imagery workstation
answers.rationale: This reverses both needs: maintainers need wireless mobility and roaming, and wired is faster for the workstation's Local Area Network (LAN) file transfers.

answers.text: Wireless for the maintainers and wired for the imagery workstation

questions.stem: Two base buildings must be linked to carry classified traffic. Security staff warn that an adversary may set up listening equipment anywhere along the route between the buildings to capture the link's signals. MSgt Rush must choose a transmission medium for the link that leaves the adversary nothing to capture. Which medium is best supported?

keywords.text: set up listening equipment anywhere along the route

answers.rationale: Shielded Twisted Pair (STP) carries electric signals, not light, so it lacks fiber's immunity to electromagnetic monitoring.
Fiber carries light instead of electric signals, so it emits no electromagnetic radiation to monitor, and as guided media it avoids unguided interception.

Laser light transmission is unguided media, so its signals are more susceptible to interception and monitoring even though it uses light.

questions.stem: Two base sites must be joined by a single cable segment that carries 100 Megabits per second (Mbps) Ethernet. answers.rationale: Multimode Fiber (MMF) supports longer segments than twisted-pair wire but stops at 2000 meters for 100 Megabits per second (Mbps) Ethernet, too short for this route.
Shielded Twisted Pair (STP) is twisted-pair wire, which supports shorter segments than Multimode Fiber (MMF), itself too short here.
Unshielded Twisted-Pair (UTP) is twisted-pair wire, which supports shorter segments than Multimode Fiber (MMF), itself too short here.
Single-Mode Fiber (SMF) supports much longer segments than any other guided media, while Multimode Fiber (MMF) stops at 2000 meters for 100 Megabits per second (Mbps) Ethernet.

questions.stem: A base web server will not open when an airman types its name into a browser. MSgt Rush then pings the server's Internet Protocol (IP) address from the same computer, and every request gets a reply with no packet loss. MSgt Rush must choose the next tool to narrow down the fault. Which tool is best supported?

keywords.text: every request gets a reply with no packet loss

answers.rationale: tracert traces the route to a destination through the routers encountered, but the ping replies already show that route to the server works.
netstat displays a computer's active network connections and their states; it does not translate a server's name into its address.
Ping replies show the path to the server's Internet Protocol (IP) address works, and nslookup translates domain names to IP addresses, the step still untested.
arp views or edits the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache of recently contacted devices' addresses; it does not translate a server's name.

questions.stem: An airman pings a printer on the same local network and gets replies. The airman then pings the Internet Protocol (IP) address of a server at another base and gets no replies at all. Before calling the other base, MSgt Rush must choose the next tool to narrow down the fault. Which tool is best supported?

answers.rationale: Local ping replies show this computer's connection works, and tracert lists each router encountered toward the server with its Round-Trip Time (RTT).
nslookup translates domain names to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, but these pings went to the server's IP address and needed no translation.
netstat displays this computer's active network connections and their states; it does not show where along the path the traffic stops.
A port scanner identifies open ports and services on a host; it does not show where along the path the traffic stops.

questions.stem: Users in a squadron say large downloads from an Internet site take far longer than their service is supposed to allow. An airman pings the site by its name, and every request gets a reply, with no packet loss and normal latency. MSgt Rush must choose the next tool to measure the problem the users describe. Which tool is best supported?

keywords.text: no packet loss and normal latency

answers.rationale: tracert lists the routers encountered on the route to a destination, but the ping replies already show the site is reachable without loss.
A protocol analyzer captures individual packets to examine their protocols, addresses and size; it does not measure connection speed.
nslookup translates domain names to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, and the replies to pings sent by name show that translation works.
Ping replies show no packet loss or latency problem, and a bandwidth speed tester measures download and upload speed and compares it to expected speeds.

questions.stem: A fiber optic cable runs underground beneath the flight line between two buildings, and the link between them is down. An earlier test has already shown that the light reaching the far end is far too weak. MSgt Rush must choose a tool that tells the crew where along the run to dig. Which tool is best supported?

keywords.text: the light reaching the far end is far too weak

answers.rationale: A tone generator emits an audible tone into one end of a cable so a probe can trace it; it does not measure light.
An Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) checks for breaks in fiber optic cable by measuring the light reflected off the break, while an optical power meter only measures signal strength.

answers.text: An optical power meter with an optical light source
answers.rationale: An optical power meter works with an optical light source to measure signal strength and detect excessive attenuation, which the earlier test already showed; it does not locate a break along the run.
A digital multimeter uses metal-tipped probes to measure voltage, resistance and continuity in electrical circuits, not light in fiber optic cable.

questions.stem: On one workstation, every nslookup query an airman runs fails, while the workstations beside it get answers to the very same queries. MSgt Rush wants to look at that one workstation first, before changing anything on it. Which tool is best supported?

keywords.text: the workstations beside it get answers to the very same queries

answers.rationale: Failing nslookup queries point to a Domain Name System (DNS) problem, and ipconfig shows the local host's configuration, including its DNS settings.
arp views or edits the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache of recently contacted devices' addresses, not the workstation's name resolution settings.
netstat displays active network connections and their states; it does not list the workstation's Domain Name System (DNS) settings.
tracert traces the route to a destination through routers; it does not show this workstation's Domain Name System (DNS) settings.

questions.stem: A workstation will not connect to the network. An airman checks its patch cable with a cable tester, and the tester finds nothing wrong with the cable. With the same cable plugged back in, the link still fails. MSgt Rush must choose the next tool to narrow down the fault. Which tool is best supported?

keywords.text: the tester finds nothing wrong with the cable

answers.rationale: A digital multimeter measures voltage, resistance and continuity in electrical circuits; the cable's continuity is already confirmed and it does not self-test a port.
A tone generator and probe trace and identify a cable by its tone, but this cable is already identified and tested.
The cable tester clears the cable, and a loopback adapter tests the workstation's network port by letting the device send information to itself.
A crimper secures cable ends to connectors with mechanical pressure, but the tester already shows this cable's pinouts are correct.

questions.stem: Switches in one wiring closet keep failing, and an airman finds that the closet runs hot. MSgt Rush wants the Network Monitoring System (NMS) to give warning before the next switch fails, not only a record of it afterward. Which setup best meets this need?

keywords.text: give warning before the next switch fails

answers.text: Monitor the closet temperature and the switch fans, and alert on them
answers.rationale: Most network monitoring tools also monitor switch fans and wiring-closet temperature, and alerts notify administrators when something goes wrong.

answers.text: Monitor the switches' Central Processing Unit (CPU) and memory, and alert on them
answers.rationale: Central Processing Unit (CPU) and memory are among the big 5 starting monitors; they leave out the fans and closet temperature behind these failures.

answers.text: Monitor the closet temperature and the switch fans, and review their historical reports
answers.rationale: Report deals with real-time and historical reporting; notifying administrators when something goes wrong is the job of alerts.

answers.text: Monitor the switches' Central Processing Unit (CPU) and memory, and review their historical reports
answers.rationale: Central Processing Unit (CPU) and memory are big 5 monitors that leave out the fans and closet temperature, and reports do not notify administrators.

questions.stem: Users report that pages from a base web server load slowly. An airman pings the server, and every request gets a reply with no packet loss. MSgt Rush asks which Network Monitoring System (NMS) statistic best tracks this complaint. Which statistic should the airman examine?

keywords.text: every request gets a reply with no packet loss

answers.rationale: Availability asks whether a service or device is up and responding to requests, and the ping replies already show the server responding.
Route analytics covers the routes and hops that requests travel through between client and server, not how fast each request is processed.
Disk utilization is one of the big 5 device monitors; it does not tell how fast each request is processed.
Response time tracks how fast each request is processed; ping already monitors availability and every request got a reply, so speed is the open question.

questions.stem: Two metal panels of an equipment rack are welded together so that current crosses the joint with very little opposition. Which practice has joined the panels?

answers.rationale: Grounding is a conductive path between the earth and a grounded object, not a joint between two panels.
Bonding is the establishment of a low-impedance path between two metal surfaces, and bonds can be made by welding.
Shielding is a noise control measure for local noise sources or media, not a metal joint.
Filtering is a noise control measure for local noise sources or media, not a metal joint.

questions.stem: While a vacuum cleaner runs nearby, a television shows lines across its picture and its sound becomes distorted. Which problem does the vacuum cause?

answers.rationale: Impedance is the opposition electricity faces when it flows through something that is not a perfect conductor.
Triboelectricity is the charge that friction develops, commonly referred to as static electricity.
Electromagnetic Interference (EMI), also called electrical noise, disrupts electricity; a household vacuum cleaner is an example source.

questions.stem: Rubbing two different materials together leaves one of them holding an electrical charge until it touches something. Which term names the charge that this rubbing produces?

answers.rationale: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) is the sudden flow of electricity between two charged objects, not the resting charge.
Transient voltage is brief surges of electricity, usually from components suddenly releasing stored electricity.
Friction develops a charge called triboelectricity, commonly referred to as static electricity or electricity at rest.
Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) is a disruption in electricity that produces fluctuations in voltage or current.

questions.stem: A company builds radios to a defense document that lists exactly which methods and materials the armed services require. Which publication type is it?

A Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) implements policy by providing detailed procedures for carrying out that policy.

keywords.text: hardened against attack in one standard way

answers.rationale: A Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) is a cybersecurity methodology for standardizing security protocols within networks and computers.

answers.rationale: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) allows you to view websites using a web browser.

answers.rationale: Shielding is a noise control measure for local noise sources or media.

questions.stem: A defense policy is already set, and an airman needs the publication that spells out, step by step, how to put it into practice. Which publication type is it?

keywords.text: conversation started, kept in step and then ended

keywords.text: recovers the missing data end to end

questions.stem: A workstation drops off the network, so an airman first makes sure its cord is seated and it still has power. Which Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layer is this?

keywords.text: makes sure its cord is seated and it still has power

answers.rationale: When a networking problem occurs, many professionals go right to the Physical layer to check cables and power plugs.

questions.stem: An airman clicks a link in a web browser, and a new page of a website loads. Which protocol carries this page request and reply?

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is planning addresses for a small office that will hold only a handful of hosts. Which address class is intended for networks like this?

questions.stem: An airman checks a host on the base network whose address has the value 172 in its first octet. Which address class does that address belong to?

A multifunction Access Point (AP) combines an access point with a switch, a router and sometimes a modem.

questions.stem: During a field exercise, MSgt Rush links a laptop straight to an airman's laptop, with no other wireless equipment between them. Which network type is this?

questions.stem: Dozens of unlabeled cables enter a wiring closet, and an airman must pick out the one that runs to a single office wall jack. Which tool should the airman use?

keywords.text: pick out the one that runs to a single office wall jack

questions.stem: During a security assessment, MSgt Rush asks an airman to list which services a computer is offering and leaving open to the network. Which software tool fits?

answers.rationale: A protocol analyzer captures and examines individual packets; it does not list a host's services.

questions.stem: A distant site is slow to reach, so an airman wants to see each stop on the way there and the delay at each one. Which command shows this?

questions.stem: A computer cannot reach anything beyond its own network, so an airman wants to view the address and gateway settings set up on that computer. Which command shows them?
