Wrong: a Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server transfers and stores mail, and attaching the logs to messages was ruled out.
Wrong: a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) server delivers site data to browsers, and posting the logs for browsers was ruled out.
Wrong: a cloud server delivers pooled resources from a provider; it is not described as moving files between two computers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is setting up a server that will transfer and store messages for a wing across its Local Area Networks (LANs), its Wide Area Networks (WANs), and the Internet. Before opening the firewall, MSgt Rush must know which protocol this server uses for that traffic. Which protocol should MSgt Rush plan for?

answers.rationale: Wrong: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) carries communication between browsers and web servers, not stored messages.
Correct: mail servers, which transfer and store mail across networks and the Internet, use Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP).
Wrong: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) moves files between computers; it is not the protocol mail servers use.
Wrong: the Telnet protocol lets users log on to a remote computer; it does not carry stored messages.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's unit owns one physical server in an off-site data center and manages its hardware itself, with no outside provider. Three sections each want to administer their own system services as if they had complete control of a server, and their workloads shift every week. Which approach meets these needs?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a cloud server and its infrastructure are managed by the cloud provider, but this unit manages its own hardware.
Wrong: a terminal server supplies applications to remote clients; it does not give each section control of its own server.
Correct: a virtual server converts one physical server into multiple Virtual Machines (VMs), each administered as if in complete control.
Wrong: a multi-purpose server performs several functions, but the sections would share one system rather than each controlling its own.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches network traffic while an airman opens the base's home page. The browser sends a request, and the server loads a file from its disk and transfers it across the network back to the browser. MSgt Rush needs to name the protocol that carries this exchange between the browser and the server. Which protocol is it?

answers.rationale: Wrong: File Transfer Protocol (FTP) moves files between computers, but it is not described for browser requests to web servers.
Wrong: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) is the protocol mail servers use, not browsers.
Wrong: the Telnet protocol lets users log on to a remote computer and run programs, not load web pages.
Correct: communication between a client's browser and a web server uses Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP).

questions.stem: A squadron needs processing power, storage, and applications that many airmen can reach on demand from anywhere, delivered remotely over the Internet. MSgt Rush has no staff to maintain hardware, so the squadron must not have to manage the server or any of the infrastructure behind it. Which server type fits this need?

answers.rationale: Correct: a cloud server and all associated infrastructure are managed by the cloud provider, such as Microsoft Azure.
Wrong: a virtual server lets each section administer its own services, which still leaves the squadron managing them.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host on the Local Area Network (LAN) that the squadron would run itself.
Wrong: an application server runs specific programs as middleware; it is not described as managed by an outside provider.

questions.stem: A plant runs a self-contained industrial network with no link to outside networks. MSgt Rush needs to log on remotely from one computer to the plant's devices and execute tasks on them as if sitting at each machine. Because the network is closed, a server type with a known security weakness is acceptable here. Which server type is typically used in this setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a terminal server supplies applications to thin clients and workstations; it is not described as limited to industrial networks.
Correct: a Telnet server is typically used only in industrial and self-contained networks because it is not secure.
Wrong: a virtual server re-creates a physical server as Virtual Machines (VMs); it does not provide remote logon to devices.
Wrong: a proxy server mediates between clients and external servers, and this network has no outside link.

questions.stem: A small detachment has one server for six airmen. It hosts the detachment's website, it also handles all printing on the local network, and MSgt Rush sits at it each morning to do administrator work. A new airman asks how to describe this server's role on the network. Which description fits it?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a single-purpose server provides specific services and nothing else, and end users do not sit at it.
Wrong: it does host a website, but a web server alone serves only web pages, not printing and administrator work.
Correct: a multi-purpose (non-dedicated) web server may also act as a print server or the administrator's workstation.
Wrong: a workstation is a personal computer used by a client; this machine serves the site and printing to others.

questions.stem: Five airmen at a deployed site link their laptops with no server present. Each laptop shares one folder with the others while keeping the rest of its files inaccessible, and when one laptop requests a file from another, the second laptop answers as the server. No laptop has more authority than another. Which network model are the airmen using?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a client-server model relies on a dedicated server as intermediary, and this site has no server.
Wrong: a multi-purpose server is one server doing several tasks, but this site has no server at all.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that clients connect through; no such host exists here.
Correct: in a peer-to-peer model there are no dedicated servers, and each computer can share only some of its resources.

questions.stem: An airman will be posted for weeks at a remote site that has no network and no domain at all. MSgt Rush must issue a device that has its own processor, memory, and drive and that will never connect to a central server during that time. Which device can function completely on its own in that setting?

answers.rationale: Wrong: a thin client relies on the central server for applications, processing, and memory.
Correct: a workstation has all components and can function completely independently of a server or network.
Wrong: a thick client works in a client-server configuration and still pulls data from the central server occasionally.
Wrong: a terminal server is a host that supplies applications to remote clients; it is not a device issued to an airman.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush checks an airman's workstation while it runs a mission planning application opened through a web portal. Only screen images, mouse movements, and keystrokes cross the network, the workstation's processor shows no load from the application, and the whole squadron uses the one copy installed on a shared Windows server. Which desktop virtualization type is in use?

keywords.text: one copy installed on a shared Windows server

answers.rationale: Only the graphical interface, mouse, and keyboard are shared, with no processing on the client and one shared application instance.
This type hosts a dedicated Operating System (OS) Virtual Machine (VM) for each client, not one shared copy.
This model sends portions of the program code to the client, so the client would show processing.
This type moves profiles, settings, and data to a central share; it is not an application delivery method.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must give deployed airmen access to graphics-heavy imagery software from tablets. The design needs hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing through a secure connection from any device, and each airman's desktop must stay totally separate from every other desktop on the server, with permissions customized for each airman. Which desktop virtualization type fits?

answers.text: Presentation virtualization on a shared Virtual Machine (VM)
answers.rationale: This type has users share one application instance on a shared server, so desktops are not separate.
Its hypervisor hosts a dedicated machine per client and enables hardware-based Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) sharing from any device.
This type decouples profiles and data from the Operating System (OS); it does not host separate desktops.
This model delivers program portions on demand to a client; it does not host separate desktops.

questions.stem: An airman works at a physical desktop in the squadron office on Monday, a virtual desktop from a deployed laptop on Wednesday, and a different physical workstation on Friday. MSgt Rush wants the airman's settings and data kept in a central data share and applied at every one of these, including the physical machines. Which approach meets this need?

answers.rationale: This type hosts dedicated Virtual Machines (VM) on a server; it does not reach the physical desktops.
This type shows a shared server application to clients; it does not manage profiles on physical desktops.
It decouples profile, settings, and data from the Operating System (OS), stores them centrally, and also works on physical desktops.
This type runs applications from central servers; it does not store a person's settings and data centrally.

questions.stem: An airman launches a large engineering program on a laptop that never had it installed. A packet capture shows only a small part of the program's code arriving at first, with more portions sent across the network when the airman opens other features. The program then runs on the laptop's own processor. Which delivery model is MSgt Rush seeing?

keywords.text: small part of the program's code

answers.rationale: This type processes nothing on the client and sends only a picture of the application.
This type runs applications on central servers and serves them up, rather than sending code portions on demand.
This type hosts a full dedicated desktop Virtual Machine (VM) on a server for each client.
Most applications need only a small portion of their code, so portions are offered across the network whenever required.

questions.stem: A flight line test set uses older industrial software that runs only on a legacy Operating System (OS). MSgt Rush must move the workstation to a current OS that receives up-to-date security patches, keep using the old software, and be able to transfer that software between computers on removable media without installing it. Which approach meets all three needs?

answers.rationale: It runs applications in foreign environments, keeps the new patched Operating System (OS), and makes them portable on removable media.
This architecture modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not make software portable on removable media.
This architecture presents emulated devices such as a switch to a guest server, not portable legacy software.
This model sends program portions across a network on demand; it does not carry software on removable media.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must run twenty small Linux web applications on one Linux server. Each application needs isolation from the others, new instances must come online extremely fast from the same base set, and no application needs its own full copy of an Operating System (OS). Which approach should MSgt Rush choose?

answers.rationale: Each of these replicates an entire Operating System (OS) for its application, so each is larger and slower to bring online.
They share one host kernel, spin up from the same base set very fast, and still isolate applications.
Each guest still runs its own modified Operating System (OS) kernel inside a Virtual Machine (VM).
This architecture presents emulated hardware to a guest server; it does not remove the guest Operating System (OS).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans to move several web services off their Virtual Machines (VM) onto one server whose host kernel allows multiple isolated user-space instances, to gain efficiency. The services run different software stacks today. An airman asks what flexibility the squadron gives up in exchange for that efficiency. Which limitation comes with this architecture?

answers.text: The guest kernel must be modified for hyper calls
answers.rationale: Modified guest kernels that use hyper calls belong to para-virtualization, a different architecture.

answers.text: The hypervisor steals resources from its guests
answers.rationale: Resource stealing is a drawback of a hosted Type 2 hypervisor running on a busy host Operating System (OS).

answers.text: Each instance must match the host server's system
answers.rationale: This method gives greater efficiency but less flexibility: the container Operating System (OS) must match the host server's.

answers.text: Built-in device drivers limit the hardware support
answers.rationale: Limited built-in device drivers are a drawback of a bare-metal Type 1 hypervisor.

questions.stem: A training network needs a router between two subnets, but the squadron has no budget to buy, power, and maintain another physical device. MSgt Rush sets up the server so that the hypervisor presents a router to one guest virtual server, no matter what physical hardware is installed in the host. Which server virtualization architecture is this?

answers.rationale: This lets a guest reach real host hardware through hyper calls; it does not present a simulated device.
This creates isolated user-space instances on a shared kernel; it does not present a simulated router.
This pools disks from several network storage devices; it does not present a router to a guest.
The host or hypervisor emulates hardware such as a router for the guest, saving the physical device's costs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush compares two Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. In the first, the guest Operating System (OS) is completely isolated and never interacts with the hypervisor. In the second, the guest kernel was modified, is not fully separate from the host, and processes faster by using host hardware directly. Which technique does the second machine use?

answers.rationale: Its modified guest kernel talks to the host through hyper calls, speeding processing by using host hardware directly.
This describes the first machine: the guest is completely isolated and does not interact with the hypervisor.
This presents emulated devices to a guest; it does not modify the guest kernel.
This uses containers on a shared host kernel, with no guest Operating System (OS) inside a Virtual Machine (VM).

questions.stem: An airman must test a software update against a copy of the base network, including several servers, a firewall, and workstations. The squadron has only one spare server, will not buy specialized servers for occasional testing, and the live network must not be touched. Which virtual environment does MSgt Rush set up for the airman?

answers.rationale: This is a copy of one Virtual Machine (VM) at a point in time, not a replica of a network.
It is a simulated lab reflecting a real network, replicating several machines on a single piece of hardware.
This separates applications on one shared kernel; it does not reflect a whole physical network.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image; it is not a test network.

questions.stem: Three Virtual Machines (VM) on separate physical hosts run the same squadron application. Monitoring shows one machine overloaded and slow to respond while the other two sit idle. MSgt Rush wants the regular workload divided so every machine carries a portion and the machines adjust dynamically to the application's demands. Which application of virtualization should MSgt Rush apply?

answers.rationale: This moves once-dedicated servers onto fewer hosts; it does not divide work among existing machines.
This lets software pick the best physical server for a Virtual Machine (VM) image, not divide regular work.
It divides the regular workload among machines on separate hardware so none sit idle and responsiveness improves.
This responds to catastrophic losses such as a whole data center, not an uneven daily workload.

questions.stem: A squadron runs twelve physical servers, each with one function such as a domain controller or a name server, and most of them sit underutilized. MSgt Rush must cut the number of machines to maintain and put existing resources to better use, so the twelve servers become Virtual Machines (VM) on one host. Which application of virtualization is this?

answers.rationale: This spreads one workload across machines on separate hardware; it does not reduce the number of servers.
This points software at a Virtual Machine (VM) image to pick a server; it does not merge servers.
This responds to catastrophic incidents such as losing a data center, not to underutilized servers.
One host now holds many once-dedicated, underutilized servers, increasing utilization and cutting maintenance costs.

questions.stem: On Monday one Virtual Machine (VM) crashed and was restarted, and on Tuesday a failed server's work shifted to another host with no outage. On Wednesday MSgt Rush writes a plan for a flood that could permanently destroy the entire base data center, relying on machine images captured in files. Which area does Wednesday's plan cover?

answers.rationale: It covers incidents far worse than a single crash or hardware failure, such as an entire data center lost.
This explains Tuesday's event, where the work shifted between machines on separate hardware.
This lets software pick a physical server for an image; it is not a plan for catastrophic loss.
This returns one machine to an earlier state, fitting a single crash rather than a lost data center.

questions.stem: An airman deletes a Virtual Machine (VM) that nobody could explain, and a squadron service goes down. MSgt Rush finds the host now holds far more machines than the squadron can manage, many of them unused, while storage, bandwidth, and electricity use keep climbing. Which problem has the squadron run into?

answers.text: A Virtual Machine (VM) patch management gap
answers.rationale: Missed patches expose security issues; they do not explain more machines than the squadron can track.
Machines created over time exceed management capacity, their functions are lost, and unused machines drain resources.
Change control governs approval of infrastructure changes; it does not describe too many machines to manage.
Load balancing divides work among machines; it does not create unmanaged, unused machines.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team patched the host and guest Operating Systems (OS), the web servers, and the database servers on schedule. A month later, an attacker gets in through a small open-source library bundled inside a third-party reporting tool on a guest. Logs captured the attack, and every change had been approved. Which area of virtualization security fell short?

answers.rationale: Every change had been approved, so the change control process worked as intended.
The logs captured the attack, so the audit trail did its job.
Updates focused on big targets while smaller third-party and open-source components were forgotten.
Nothing shows wrong host accounts or access; the attacker came in through a neglected component.

questions.stem: An airman's desktop has uncommon hardware whose drivers come only with its installed Operating System (OS). The airman must keep that OS and add a Virtual Machine (VM) that runs a different OS for a Windows-only tool, accepting some loss of VM performance. Which choice fits this desktop?

answers.rationale: This installs directly on hardware in place of the host Operating System (OS) and has limited built-in drivers.
Containers share the host kernel, so they cannot run a different Operating System (OS) than the host.
This modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not leave the installed Operating System (OS) handling drivers.
It runs on the host Operating System (OS), which handles drivers, giving better hardware compatibility but degraded performance.

questions.stem: A server runs a Type 1 hypervisor that hosts a Virtual Machine (VM) with a Linux distribution as its guest Operating System (OS). Inside that VM, MSgt Rush creates several containers that all share the Linux kernel. An airman asks how the Linux OS should be described in relation to those containers. Which term applies?

answers.rationale: The Linux guest serves as the host Operating System (OS) for containers that share its kernel.
Nothing here runs on top of the Linux system to create Virtual Machines (VM); the containers share its kernel.
The bare-metal role belongs to the Type 1 hypervisor installed on the server hardware.
Para-virtualization modifies a guest kernel for hyper calls; it does not describe the containers' shared kernel.

questions.stem: A host server runs today with only two of one component, which works but falls below the recommended amount. MSgt Rush must now place its Virtual Machines (VM) on three separate networks, keep service if one link fails, and raise speed and bandwidth. Which component should MSgt Rush add to the host?

answers.rationale: This card connects a monitor when a host lacks integrated graphics; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.
Two can operate a host, but more are recommended for bandwidth, redundancy, speed, and separating traffic.
These raise processor efficiency for virtualization; they do not split traffic onto separate networks.
Storage limits how many machines are stored and run; it does not separate traffic or add redundancy.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports a forest with two domains. Each domain controller holds the objects and object attributes unique to its own domain. Airmen in the first domain now need to locate and use a shared printer published in the second domain. Which server must MSgt Rush make sure is available so that computers in one domain can find resources in the other?

keywords.text: shared printer published in the second domain

answers.rationale: A member server serves dedicated purposes such as file and print; it does not locate objects across domains.
It holds a partial replica of every object in every domain of the forest, so computers in one domain can locate resources in another.
Each domain controller holds only objects unique to its own domain, so it alone cannot locate the second domain's printer.
A domain client is a computer that uses resources; it does not let other computers locate resources in other domains.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush supports one domain whose users work at two bases. A slow Wide Area Network (WAN) link joins the two bases, and each base has its own squadrons and administrators. MSgt Rush wants every user to stay in the same domain while Active Directory (AD) reflects the slow link between the bases. Which component should MSgt Rush create for each base?

answers.rationale: Windows encourages sites when a network is divided by a slow link, and both sites can be part of the same domain.
A child domain would split the users into separate domains, but they must stay in one domain.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it does not reflect a slow link inside one domain.
A forest is the collection of domain trees at the top of the structure; it does not mark a slow link.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush joins a new Windows Server to the squadron's domain so that it can host the squadron's web pages. The server must belong to the domain, but it must not hold a writable copy of the domain's Active Directory (AD) information and must not authenticate logons. Which role should MSgt Rush give the new server?

answers.rationale: Every domain controller holds a complete, writable copy of the domain's directory information and authenticates users.
A global catalog server is normally a domain controller and stores replicas of directory objects.
A domain client runs a user's desktop environment to reach resources; it does not host web pages for the squadron.
It belongs to a domain without being the domain controller and is used for dedicated purposes such as web servers.

questions.stem: A small base runs one domain with a single domain controller, plus a member server for file and print services. When the domain controller fails, no airman can log on to the domain, though the file server keeps running. MSgt Rush wants the next failure of one server to leave domain logons working. Which addition does MSgt Rush need?

keywords.text: no airman can log on to the domain

answers.rationale: A member server is not a domain controller, so it cannot authenticate users when the only one fails.
A site maps the physical structure of the network; adding one does not add a server that authenticates users.
Networks normally have more than one, so if one fails others store the directory structure and authenticate users.
A domain tree is a collection of domains sharing a namespace; it adds no backup for this domain's logons.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush changes the replication topology data on a domain controller in AF.Domain. Later, MSgt Rush signs on to a domain controller in Medical.Domain, a different domain in the same forest, and finds the same change there. Which directory partition holds the data that MSgt Rush changed?

answers.rationale: It contains replication topology data replicated throughout the forest, and every domain controller in the forest has a replica.
The domain partition stores users, computers, and groups for one specific domain, not data shared by another domain.
The schema partition stores class and attribute definitions for objects, not replication topology data.
The forest root domain is the first domain created in the forest; it is not a directory partition.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must add a badge number to the types of information that a user account object can hold. The change has to reach every user object in the forest, existing and future, not only the users of one domain or one Organizational Unit (OU). Which part of Active Directory (AD) defines this for the user object type?

answers.rationale: The configuration partition stores configuration objects and replication topology, not the definition of a user object type.
Each type of object is defined through it, the template of attributes that sets the types of information an object can hold.
The domain partition stores the users and other objects of one domain, not the definitions of object types.
An Organizational Unit (OU) holds users, groups, and computers; it does not define what a user object can hold.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush creates user accounts for two airmen in one Organizational Unit (OU). Both accounts are user objects of the same type, and Active Directory (AD) keeps them as two separate entities. MSgt Rush reviews their attributes to see how AD distinguishes the two objects. Which statement describes what MSgt Rush finds?

keywords.text: user objects of the same type

answers.rationale: All objects of the same type or class have the same set of attributes.
Objects of the same class are distinguished from each other by having different values for at least one attribute.
Syntaxes belong to the schema for the object type, and both objects share that same type.
Some attributes, such as First Name for a user object, are required to have values.

questions.stem: In an Organizational Unit (OU), MSgt Rush finds a printer object and several user objects. MSgt Rush tries to move one of the user objects into the printer object, but Active Directory (AD) does not allow it, although moving the same user object into another OU works. Which description fits the printer object?

keywords.text: move one of the user objects into the printer object

answers.rationale: A container object can hold other objects, but the printer object could not hold the user object.
A child domain is a domain created after the root, and domains are container objects that hold other objects.
It is found in containers such as Organizational Units (OUs) and cannot contain other directory objects.
The forest root is the first domain created in the forest, and domains can hold other objects.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is deploying a new Active Directory (AD) forest for a base. The plan calls for one domain used only to administer the forest and three regional domains for the squadrons, each with its own Organizational Units (OUs). Before building any of the regional domains, which domain must MSgt Rush already have created?

keywords.text: building any of the regional domains

answers.rationale: It must be created before any of the regional domains and provides the foundation for the infrastructure.
Child domains are created after the root, so a regional child domain cannot come before it.
A domain tree is a collection of domains, not a single domain that must exist before the regional ones.
Squadron domains are regional domains, and none of those may be built ahead of the foundation domain.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush manages two domain trees, AF.Domain and Medical.Domain, that share one global catalog and one directory schema. Each domain in them has its own security policies and its own security boundary. MSgt Rush must name the outermost boundary of the directory service, within which the users and computers of both trees are accessible. Which structure is it?

keywords.text: outermost boundary of the directory service

answers.rationale: Each domain is a security boundary for its own objects, but it does not hold both trees.
A site maps the physical structure of the network and is defined by subnets, not a security boundary.
A domain tree holds domains sharing one namespace, and the two trees here have different namespaces.
It represents the security boundary within which users, computers, and groups are accessible and is the outermost boundary.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a third Domain Name System (DNS) server for a branch site. The site's two existing name servers will keep sending it updates, but the new server will hold no zone of its own, and its answers must never count as authoritative for the zone. Which name server role fits the new server?

answers.rationale: It holds no zone, is authoritative for no zone, and receives updates from primary and secondary servers.
This server holds a zone copy and can answer authoritatively for its zone.
This server holds the master zone file and is authoritative for its zone.
These servers form the upper-most layer of the namespace, not a branch site role.

questions.stem: The primary name server for a zone at MSgt Rush's site goes offline for repairs. Clients must still get authoritative answers for that zone from another server at the site that holds its own copy of the zone, received from the primary before the outage. Which server at the site can give those answers?

answers.rationale: This server keeps copies of zone information but is not authoritative for any zone.
It obtains its zone files from the primary and is authoritative, so it can answer queries for its zone.
These servers sit at the top of the namespace and do not hold the site's zone.
These servers resolve names such as .com and do not hold the site's zone.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must change the Mail Exchanger (MX) record for a zone that three name servers at the site handle. Each server answers lookups for the zone, and the change must reach all of them through the normal replication between servers, not by editing each one in turn. On which server must MSgt Rush enter the change?

answers.rationale: Its zone copies are read only and come from another server by zone transfer.
This server holds no zone information and only receives updates from other servers.
It holds the master copy of the zone file and passes zone information to the other servers.
These servers form the top layer of the namespace and do not hold the site's zone.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush updates an Address (A) record on the primary name server. At a second site, the secondary name server still holds its read-only text copy of the zone without the update, and an airman there cannot edit that copy. Which process must run before the secondary's copy of the zone includes the new record?

answers.rationale: Expiry removes cached entries from a local server; it does not update a zone copy.
The secondary zone database can only be updated by the primary server through this process.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush moves a web server to a new Internet Protocol (IP) address and updates its Address (A) record on the primary name server. An airman's local name server had answered a lookup for that site shortly before, and the airman keeps reaching the old address. Which setting decides how long the local name server keeps giving that stored answer?

answers.rationale: This parameter defines how long an entry remains cached on the local name server.
This record holds admin details for the zone, not how long a cached answer lasts.
Zone transfers synchronize primary and secondary zones, not cached answers on a local server.
This record identifies servers to contact for a domain, not how long answers stay cached.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush watches the local Domain Name System (DNS) server resolve rhope-ops.github.io for an airman. The root server returns only the name of the .io server, and the local server then sends its own request to that .io server. The .io server returns the name of the github.io server, and again the local server asks that server directly. Which query type is MSgt Rush watching?

answers.rationale: In this type each server passes the request on to the next server down.
The local server keeps responsibility and asks each server in the hierarchy itself.
This lookup resolves an address to a name, but the airman asked for a name.

questions.stem: An airman's client asks the local Domain Name System (DNS) server for rhope-ops.github.io. The local server sends the request to the root server, the root server sends it on to the .io server, and that server sends it on to the github.io server. The reply then travels back through each server in reverse order to the client. Which query type did the client start?

answers.rationale: In this type the local server asks each server itself instead of each server passing it on.
Each server takes responsibility and delegates the request to the next server down.
This lookup resolves an address to a name, but the client asked for a name.

questions.stem: A new Domain Name System (DNS) server at MSgt Rush's site already resolves every hostname to its Internet Protocol (IP) address for clients, and name service works without problems. MSgt Rush now sets up authentication of email traffic sources, which needs a zone type that normal operation does not require. Which zone type must MSgt Rush add?

answers.rationale: The server already resolves hostnames to addresses, so this zone type is in place.
This read-only copy of a primary zone does not add a new lookup direction.
This master zone file already supports the server's hostname lookups.
This zone type is not required for operation but is required to authenticate email traffic sources.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush builds a new Domain Name System (DNS) server whose only zone so far answers requests that give an Internet Protocol (IP) address and ask for the hostname. The server does not function properly yet. Which zone type must the server have at least one of before it can function properly?

answers.rationale: The server must have at least one forward lookup database to function properly.
The server already has this zone type, and it is not required for operation.
This read-only copy comes from a primary zone and is not the required database.
Cached entries expire and are not a zone database the server requires.

questions.stem: Two Domain Name System (DNS) servers at MSgt Rush's site keep the same zone as text files. On the first server, an airman can open the file and change a record. On the second server, the file can be updated only by the first server through a synchronization process. Which database is stored on the first server?

answers.rationale: This read-only copy matches the second server, which only the primary can update.
It is the master copy of the zone database file, stored as a standard text file.
Cached entries are kept for a limited time and are not an editable zone file.

Correct: this step means presenting information about yourself to a system, such as a username or a smartcard.

questions.stem: An airman was permitted to use the virtual private network from home over a weekend, and each logon succeeded. On Monday, MSgt Rush must show how long each session lasted and how much bandwidth the airman consumed. Which of the centralized logon services holds this record?

answers.rationale: Authorization granted access and set the permitted tasks; it does not track the resources used.
Authentication verified the credentials at each logon; it does not log session length.
Correct: accounting logs activity and tracks resources such as access time and bandwidth consumed during a session.
Identification is presenting a username or smartcard; it records nothing about the session.

questions.stem: During the testing phase, MSgt Rush's team runs a tool that fills every field of a new logon form with thousands of random, malformed entries and records each time the application crashes or leaks memory. The goal is to find bugs before deployment. Which process is the team performing?

answers.rationale: Input validation is a coding practice that makes entered data give the desired result; it is not random testing.
Correct: random invalid data is input into fields during testing to check for crashes, memory leaks and other bugs.
Application hardening disables features that are not necessary; it does not feed data into fields.
A configuration baseline sets software options with security in mind; it is not a test.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush's team must build a scheduling application for a unit that expects to change its requirements after seeing each working piece. The team needs a model that allows going back to earlier steps and releases the application in smaller modules. Which plan should MSgt Rush adopt?

answers.text: Agile, a module about every four weeks
answers.rationale: Correct: Agile allows backtracking, and each sprint lasts approximately four weeks before its module is released.

answers.text: Waterfall, a module about every four weeks
answers.rationale: Waterfall does not permit backtracking, so it does not fit a team that must go back to earlier steps.

answers.text: Agile, a module about every six months
answers.rationale: Agile fits, but its sprints are described as lasting approximately four weeks, not six months.
Waterfall finishes each phase before the next and does not permit going back, which the unit needs.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush reviews a new web form after a hacker typed quotation marks and semicolons into the name field and made the application run commands it was never meant to run. The software is fully patched, and unneeded features are already disabled. Which good practice was left out of the form?

answers.rationale: Unneeded features were already disabled, so application hardening was in place.
The software was fully patched, so this practice was in place.
Correct: this practice ensures that no possible keyboard characters leave room for manipulation by hackers.
This prevention concerns unexpired cookies taken by code on another page, not characters typed into a field.

questions.stem: An airman checks a web account on a shared computer in the base library and leaves without clearing anything. Later, MSgt Rush opens a text file that the website stored on that computer and can read the airman's logon information and saved preferences. Which application vulnerability does this show?

keywords.text: text file that the website stored

answers.rationale: Correct: websites store small text files with preferences and logon information, and anyone who opens them can see it.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) injects malicious code into a web application, and nothing was injected here.
Scripting runs lists of commands that modify a system without input; no script ran here.
ActiveX controls can take full system access; they are not stored files of preferences.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush tests a server by inserting a disc into its optical drive and restarting it, trying to load another Operating System (OS) that would bypass the server's security controls. The startup settings still allow booting from the disc, yet the attempt fails because the files on the disc were never digitally signed. Which feature stopped the attempt?

answers.rationale: Full Disk Encryption (FDE) encrypts the drive's contents in case of theft or loss; it does not check signatures.
A Trusted Platform Module (TPM) stores the keys used to encrypt data; it does not check bootup files.
A Hardware Security Module (HSM) holds cryptographic processors on an add-on card; it does not check bootup files.
Correct: this feature lets only digitally signed bootup files run, which prevents booting a different Operating System (OS).

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must add hardware cryptographic processing to an older server that has no built-in module for storing encryption keys. The only option is to fit an add-on device into an open expansion slot so that the cryptographic processors live on it. Which device is MSgt Rush installing?

answers.rationale: A Trusted Platform Module (TPM) stores the keys used for Full Disk Encryption (FDE); it is not described as an add-on card.
Correct: cryptographic processors can be stored on a separate card installed on a system, and this module is an add-on device.
Full Disk Encryption (FDE) is a way to encrypt a whole drive, not a device fitted into a slot.
The Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) chip holds code that interfaces with hardware, not added cryptographic processors.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must send every web request from a squadron's locked-down workstations through a new proxy server. No program can be installed on the workstations, and their browser settings cannot be changed. MSgt Rush is allowed to change one network setting on each workstation, and airmen should keep thinking that setting refers to the router. Which proxy solution fits this situation?

answers.rationale: A reverse proxy carries requests from Internet systems in to internal servers, not workstation requests out.
A transparent proxy needs no client software; the default gateway setting simply points to the proxy server.
A nontransparent proxy requires a proxy client or agent and application settings on each workstation.
Installing an agent on each workstation is not possible here, since no program can be installed.

questions.stem: A partner unit's systems on the Internet need to send requests to the squadron's internal mail server. MSgt Rush wants that traffic to travel through one proxy, which checks each request for malicious content before passing it to the mail server. The squadron's workstations already reach websites through their own proxy. Which proxy does MSgt Rush add for the partner unit's requests?

answers.rationale: A forward proxy retrieves Internet resources for internal clients; the requests here travel the other way.
A transparent proxy changes how internal clients reach the Internet through their default gateway.
A nontransparent proxy needs an agent on internal clients for their outbound requests.
A reverse proxy lets Internet systems request internal servers and checks requests are not malicious before forwarding.

questions.stem: An airman maintains a project folder on a New Technology File System (NTFS) drive. MSgt Rush wants the airman to open, edit, delete and run files there, and also to decide by themselves which new teammates get access to the folder, without asking MSgt Rush each time. Which NTFS permission is the least that MSgt Rush can assign to cover all of this?

keywords.text: least that MSgt Rush can assign

answers.rationale: Full Control gives every possible permission, including the ability to change the folder's permissions.
Modify allows reading, executing, deleting, listing and writing, but not changing permissions for teammates.
Write allows changing file contents and creating files, but not deleting, running or granting access.
Read and execute allows opening and running files, but not editing, deleting or granting access.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush secures a folder on a Windows server with New Technology File System (NTFS) permissions for a flight's airmen. When an airman logs on at the server, the folder opens as expected. Airmen at their own workstations across the network, however, cannot find the folder at all. Which step has MSgt Rush not yet completed?

answers.rationale: The New Technology File System (NTFS) permissions already work at the server, so no conversion is needed.
A standard access list filters router traffic by source address, not access to a server folder.
Shared folder permissions are the second step after New Technology File System (NTFS) permissions; they publish the folder on the network.
A Group Policy Object (GPO) changes Windows features and security settings, not folder publishing.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush finds access list 45 applied to an interface on a Cisco router. An airman's workstation must be kept from reaching one file server while it still reaches the other servers on the network. Before editing the list, MSgt Rush checks which packet details the rules in list 45 can match on. Which details can those rules use?

answers.rationale: A list numbered between 1 and 99 is a standard access list, which filters based only on the source address.
Matching on both source and destination addresses needs a list numbered 100 and above.
Protocol information is matched by lists numbered 100 and above, not by list 45.
Port numbers are what packet-filtering firewalls check; list 45 matches less than that.

questions.stem: An airman's laptop moves between the squadron network and hotel networks that MSgt Rush does not control. MSgt Rush wants a firewall that protects that one laptop wherever it connects, and that can show a message when a program on the laptop tries to send data out to the Internet. Which kind of firewall meets this need?

answers.rationale: A network-based firewall sits at the edge of one network and does not travel with the laptop.
A host-based firewall is software installed on a single system, and most can show notifications.
Packet-filtering firewalls are a type of hardware firewall placed at a network's edge.
Stateful packet inspection firewalls are a type of hardware firewall placed at a network's edge.

questions.stem: Airmen have been launching an unapproved game, copied from a thumb drive, on squadron workstations. MSgt Rush wants one Group Policy Object (GPO) computer setting that stops the game from starting on those workstations, no matter which airman logs on. A record of who tried to start it is not needed. Which Security Settings policy does MSgt Rush configure?

answers.rationale: Account Policies configure user accounts, such as lockout and password rules, not which programs run.
Local Policies hold user rights, auditing and banners, not the list of programs allowed to run.
Advanced Audit Policy Configuration sets which events to audit; a record is not needed here.

questions.stem: The squadron runs a web server and a Domain Name System (DNS) server that anyone on the Internet must reach, plus file servers used by airmen alone. MSgt Rush deploys an external and an internal firewall and opens the needed ports on the external one. In which zone does MSgt Rush place the web and DNS servers?

keywords.text: anyone on the Internet must reach

answers.rationale: The private zone takes no traffic from other networks, so the public could not reach these servers.
An extranet serves selected organizations, while these servers must be reached by anyone.
The Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) holds servers the public must reach, such as web and Domain Name System (DNS) servers.
The public zone is any network the administrator does not control, so the servers do not go there.

questions.stem: A partner wing, and no other organization, needs to reach the squadron's supply database server over the Internet. Members of the public must not reach that server, and the partner wing's airmen must not reach the squadron's Local Area Network (LAN). In which zone does MSgt Rush place the supply database server?

answers.rationale: An extranet holds servers made accessible to selected organizations via the Internet or other public zones.
The Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) holds servers for the public, who must not reach this one.
A guest zone gives visitors Internet access and no access to other zones.
The private zone holds the squadron's Local Area Network (LAN), which the partner wing must not reach.

questions.stem: An airman on temporary duty connects a squadron laptop to a hotel's network, which MSgt Rush's team neither owns nor manages, and then opens the squadron's web server. MSgt Rush reviews the squadron firewall rules for traffic arriving from that hotel network. From the squadron's view, which zone is the hotel network part of?

answers.rationale: A guest zone is a segment the squadron creates for visitors at its own office.
The public zone is any network not controlled by the network administrator, such as the Internet.
An extranet holds the squadron's own servers for selected organizations.
A wireless zone is a segment the squadron creates for its own wireless clients.

questions.stem: During a root-level intrusion, the response team needs an outside forensic lab that the base has never contacted, and an hour is lost finding someone there who will take the call. At the lessons-learned review, MSgt Rush asks whose duty it was to have that kind of contact ready before the incident ever happened. Which team member holds that duty?

answers.rationale: This role assesses the scale of the incident and knows how to correct it.
This role answers legal questions about forensics and incident response.
The team leader builds relationships with outside resources that may be called upon in special circumstances.
This role logs each incident, its cause and its solution.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is staffing a new response team for a base that runs Windows servers, Linux servers and Cisco routers. One role on the team calls for hands-on expertise that no single airman has across all three platforms. Which role is the one the response team may fill with several people, each covering a different area?

answers.rationale: The team may have several Technical Specialists covering different areas such as Windows Server, Linux and Cisco.
This role makes sure each member knows their role and builds outside relationships.
This role knows the laws and regulations for computer forensics.
This role documents the response process and logs each incident.

questions.stem: Six months after a malware outbreak was cleaned up, an airman reports a workstation showing the same strange behavior. MSgt Rush wants to see what caused the earlier outbreak and how it was finally fixed, without waiting for anyone who worked it to remember. Which team member's work should hold those details?

answers.rationale: This role assesses and corrects incidents but is not the one who logs them.
This role ensures members know their roles and builds outside relationships.
This member takes charge first and contains the incident.
The Documentation Specialist logs each incident in a database, including the cause of the problem and the solution.

questions.stem: The response team plans to image a hard drive from a laptop that a visiting agency brought onto the network. Before anyone touches it, MSgt Rush wants to know whether the organization is permitted to take forensic data from a device it does not own. The technical work is not in question. Which team member should MSgt Rush ask?

answers.rationale: This role has the technical expertise to do the work, which is not in question.
The legal advisor knows the laws and regulations the organization must follow for computer forensics and incident response.
This role documents the response process and logs incidents.
This role ensures members know their roles during an incident.

questions.stem: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) log shows hundreds of valid username and password combinations tried against a server overnight. Normal defensive mechanisms blocked every attempt, the attacker never gained access, and the activity does not look like exploratory scanning. MSgt Rush must assign a category before reporting. How is this activity labeled?

answers.rationale: This category is a user-level intrusion, which needs unauthorized access.
This category is reconnaissance, which gathers information to characterize systems and users.
Category 3 is an event: deliberate access attempts defeated by normal defenses, not exploratory scanning.
This category is for activity still under investigation, and no event is closed as it.

questions.stem: Analysis of a workstation finds software that adversaries installed without the user's knowledge. The code gives the attacker remote interactive control, but only through a normal user account with no administrative privilege. MSgt Rush must record the category before the report goes out. Which category does this activity belong in?

answers.rationale: This category covers only malicious code that gives no remote interactive control.
This category is a root-level intrusion, with credentials for administrative functions.
This category is for suspicious activity that is still being investigated.
Malicious code that allows interactive access goes in CAT 1 or CAT 2; non-privileged access is a user-level intrusion, CAT 2.

questions.stem: An infected file server has just been isolated, and the threat is contained. The operations center (OC) directs MSgt Rush to make primary and working images of the server so the data can be analyzed later in a forensically sound way. Detailed analysis has not started yet. Which record should MSgt Rush begin at this point?

answers.rationale: Preliminary response actions preserve data and begin chain of custody documentation for later analysis.
The communications focal point develops this during response and recovery.
The Air Force Cyberspace Defense (ACD) unit drafts this detailed analysis as a course of action.
This review comes after handling ends, to capture lessons learned.

questions.stem: The incident analysis is complete and the root cause is known. The local Communications Focal Point (CFP) now writes a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) that names the required actions and responsible offices for restoring the affected servers and for keeping a similar incident from happening again. Which phase of the six is the team in?

answers.rationale: This phase reviews how well the incident was handled after it ends.
In response and recovery the Communications Focal Point (CFP) develops a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) to guide system restoration.
This phase finds the technical details, root causes and potential impact; it is already complete here.
These are the immediate containment and data preservation steps after an incident is declared.

questions.stem: Weeks after the affected systems were restored, MSgt Rush leads a review that finds one course of action failed because a procedure was missing and a firewall rule set was weak. The findings go to the affected Major Command (MAJCOM) so that it can revise the failed course of action. Which phase produced these findings?

answers.rationale: This phase runs while the event is in progress to find technical details and root causes.
This phase restores systems and sets follow-up strategies; restoration is already done.
This phase categorizes the activity and sends notification messages.
The postmortem captures problems executing courses of action and missing procedures, and results go to the MAJCOM/unit.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush builds a media server from two drives, with portions of each file divided between the drives to boost performance. A week later one drive fails, and none of the stored video can be rebuilt or recovered from the drive that still works. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) level was the array using?

answers.rationale: This level mirrors data, so the working drive would still hold a full copy.
This level needs three disks and uses parity to rebuild a lost drive.
Data divided between two drives with no redundancy is permanently lost when one drive fails.
This level needs four disks and mirrors the striped data.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans an array for a fast database on an application server. Five identical drives are on hand, but the chosen level uses four of them, because it needs at least four disks and an even number of drives. Losing one drive must not lose any data. Which Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) level fits that plan?

answers.rationale: This level combines striping and mirroring, needs at least four disks and an even number of drives.
This level needs four disks but has no even-number rule, so all five could be used.
This level needs only three disks and has no even-number rule.
This level needs only two drives and is described for authentication servers.

questions.stem: A file server gets a full backup on Sunday night and a second type of backup each night from Monday to Thursday. On Friday morning, MSgt Rush sees that a report edited on Monday still has an archive bit of 1 and was copied again on every nightly run since Monday. Which type are those nightly runs?

answers.rationale: A full run clears the bit as each file is copied, so the report would read 0.
This type clears the bit, so the report would not be copied again each night.
Offsite names where copies are stored, not a type that reads the archive bit.
This type copies all changes since the last full backup and leaves the bit set.

questions.stem: A server gets a full backup on Sunday and a short nightly backup from Monday to Wednesday, each run copying less data than a differential run would. After a crash on Thursday, MSgt Rush loads Sunday's disk and then has to load the Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday disks in the order they were made. Which nightly type was used?

keywords.text: in the order they were made

answers.rationale: That restore needs only the latest full and latest differential disks, not every nightly disk.
Each run holds changes since the previous backup, so every disk is restored in order.
A full run holds all files, so one disk would restore the server.
A mirror keeps a second copy of drive data and has no nightly disks.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush runs a full backup of a file share on Sunday night. No file changes on Monday, and a differential backup runs Monday night. On Tuesday morning, MSgt Rush checks the archive bit of one file to see whether it is marked as backed up. What does the bit show, and why?

answers.text: 1, because the differential run set it again
answers.rationale: A differential run does not change the bit, and nothing set it after Sunday.

answers.text: 0, because the full backup cleared it
answers.rationale: The full backup cleared the bit on Sunday, and a zero marks the file as backed up.

answers.text: 1, because full backups ignore the bit
answers.rationale: A full backup does not rely on the bit, but it does clear it as each file is copied.

answers.text: 0, because the differential run cleared it
answers.rationale: Differential backups do not clear the archive bit.

questions.stem: During an exercise, demand on a running application climbs sharply. Because the state of every service is already known, MSgt Rush adds two servers to the application by running one script. Which benefit of configuration management does that act fall under?

answers.rationale: Adding servers to running applications falls under this benefit, which aims to make it a non-event.
That benefit covers recovering assets and rolling back, not adding servers.
That benefit concerns availability and investigating downtime, not adding servers to an application.
That outcome concerns new team members, not adding servers.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush set up a server last year, measured it, fixed the default passwords found, and declared the result as the reference for later assessments. Since then, several approved updates have been applied, and the reference no longer shows how the server is supposed to be configured. What does the reference itself now require?

answers.text: Rebuilding the server to the old reference
answers.rationale: The updates were approved, so the server is kept and the reference is changed instead.
Approved updates are not undone; the reference is what falls out of date.

answers.text: A full backup taken to replace it
answers.rationale: A backup copies data and does not change the reference used for assessments.

answers.text: Updating so that it stays current
answers.rationale: As updates are applied, the baseline configuration requires updating to keep it current.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must send a deployed team a short text file of meeting times. Anyone who intercepts the message should see only an ordinary photo of the squadron building, with no sign that anything else was sent. The team will open the photo with a password in a special application to read the times. Which method fits this plan?

answers.rationale: Steganography hides information such as a text file in a graphic file, protected by a password and read with the application.
Encryption makes data unreadable, but the scrambled message itself is still plainly visible to anyone who intercepts it.
Hashing produces a value to check that data was not altered; it does not hide one file inside another.
A digital signature proves who sent a message; it does not conceal a text file inside a picture.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush downloads a software installer from a vendor website for the help desk. The vendor page lists a long value beside the download link. After the download finishes, MSgt Rush runs the file through a tool and compares the result with the value on the page, and the two match. Which integrity method did MSgt Rush just use?

answers.rationale: A digital signature uses the sender's private key to prove the sender; no private key was used here.
Vendors list the hash value of a download so that users can run their own integrity check after downloading.
A digital certificate is an electronic file that transports keys; it is not a value compared after a download.
Encryption puts data in an unreadable format; it does not produce a value to compare with a vendor listing.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sends the flight a message that changes the duty schedule. Later, an airman questions whether the change really came from MSgt Rush. For the next schedule message, MSgt Rush wants proof of the sender that only MSgt Rush could have produced, made with a key that no one else holds. Which should MSgt Rush add to the message?

answers.rationale: A hash value shows the data was not altered in transit; it does not prove who sent it.
A digital certificate is an electronic file that transports keys; by itself it does not prove the sender of one message.
A digital signature is created with the sender's private key, which only that person has, so it proves the sender.
An encrypted channel keeps tapped traffic unreadable; it does not prove which person wrote the message.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets folder permissions on a file server so that only the finance section can open its pay files. Airmen in finance then download the files to their own computers across the base network. MSgt Rush worries that someone tapping the network could read the files while they travel. Which measure closes that gap?

answers.rationale: Permissions control which accounts reach the files, but they do not protect file contents while the files are in transit.
Hashing checks that data was not altered; it does not stop someone tapping the network from reading it.
A digital signature proves the sender of a message; it leaves the contents readable to someone tapping the line.
Encrypting data in transit ensures that someone who taps into the communication cannot read the information.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush archives a signed-off maintenance report on a storage drive in the records section. Six months later, an airman opens the report to prepare for an inspection and must be certain that no figure in it was changed while it sat on the drive. Which of the three fundamental security goals is the airman relying on?

keywords.text: no figure in it was changed

answers.rationale: Data integrity also means a stored file opened later can be trusted not to have been altered while in storage.
Confidentiality ensures only authorized persons can access and read information; it does not address changes to the data.
Availability ensures information is there when wanted; the concern here is whether the stored figures were altered.
Nonrepudiation keeps someone from disputing that they sent a message or made a change; it is not a fundamental goal.

questions.stem: The squadron file server spreads its shared drive across four disks in one chassis. One morning a disk light turns red and that disk stops responding, yet airmen keep opening their files all day. Nothing was restored from backup, and no other server took over the work. Which availability solution kept the files reachable?

answers.rationale: Clustering has another server take over the workload; here no other server took over.
With a Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID), if one drive fails, the other drives provide the missing data.
Patching applies service packs and hot fixes to reduce vulnerabilities; it does not supply data from a failed disk.
Permissions limit who can delete data; they do not keep files readable after a disk fails.

questions.stem: The base e-mail service runs on two servers that MSgt Rush has set up so that airmen see them as a single system. During a storm, the first server loses power. Airmen notice only a short pause before their mailboxes load again, now served by the second machine. Which availability solution is MSgt Rush using?

answers.rationale: Fault tolerance uses redundant drives so other drives supply data; here a whole second server took the load.
Patching applies service packs and security hot fixes; it does not move a workload to another server.
Clustering has multiple servers act as one unit so that if one server fails, the other takes over the workload.
Permissions limit who can delete data; they do not keep the mail service running when a server loses power.

questions.stem: During an evening walk-through, MSgt Rush finds an airman logged in under the airman's own account on a duty section computer, printing a stack of pamphlets for a church activity. No outside code was installed, and no one else's account was used. Under which of the three Computer Security (COMPUSEC) threat categories does this activity fall?

answers.rationale: Unauthorized access is an unauthorized person gaining access; this airman used the airman's own authorized account.
Malicious logic is code written to cause problems, such as viruses; no code was installed here.
Compromising emanations are an emitted signal concern, not one of the three threat categories of this program.
Printing church activity pamphlets on a government computer is given as an example of Fraud, Waste and Abuse.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush sets up a stand-alone computer that processes Secret data in a room with no network cable or wireless card attached. Even so, MSgt Rush has the room checked for signals that the computer, its power cable, and its monitor wiring could give off and that someone outside could pick up. Which program addresses this concern?

answers.rationale: Transient Electromagnetic Pulse Emanation Surveillance Technology (TEMPEST), formerly called Emissions Security (EMSEC), covers emitted signals, even from computers with no network connection.
Communications Security (COMSEC) applies cryptosecurity, transmission security, and physical security to communications systems, not stray emitted signals.
Computer Security (COMPUSEC) focuses on end-point security and ports, protocols, and services management.
Operations Security (OPSEC) protects critical information and indicators about friendly actions from adversary collection.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush plans a protected line that will carry unencrypted classified data between two buildings at a site with a high threat assessment. The plan places the line inside a carrier fitted with sensors that sound an alarm at the security desk if anyone tampers with it. Which countermeasure is MSgt Rush installing?

answers.rationale: A simple distribution system has a reduced level of physical protection, a carrier of any material inspected by local policy.
A hardened distribution system has significant physical protection: hardened conduit, an alarmed carrier, or a continuously viewed carrier.
Red/black separation partitions plain-text signals from encrypted signals; it is not an alarmed carrier for a line.
Transmission security means choosing the right secured system for communications, not protecting a cable run physically.

questions.stem: At a low-threat training annex, MSgt Rush runs protected data cables inside a plain wooden carrier along the hallway ceiling. The joints and access points are locked and controlled by airmen cleared to the highest level of data on the line, and the carrier is inspected under local policy. Which countermeasure is this?

answers.rationale: A hardened distribution system uses hardened conduit, an alarmed carrier, or a continuously viewed carrier, not a plain wooden one.
Red/black separation partitions plain-text signals from encrypted signals; it does not describe a cable carrier.
A simple distribution system uses a carrier of any material, such as wood, with joints secured by cleared personnel.
Transmission security means choosing the right secured system for communications, not housing cables in a carrier.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush maintains the squadron's official personnel file system, set up under an Air Force directive. It holds each member's Social Security Number, rank, marital status, and home address. A member of the public asks for part of the file. Which law prescribes how these records are handled and when access to them is denied?

answers.rationale: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) gives the public the right to request records; the request is not the governing rule here.
Information Security (INFOSEC) is a discipline protecting classified and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), not a law on records about people.
Operations Security (OPSEC) protects critical information about friendly actions; it is a process, not a law on personal records.
This act prescribes management, access, handling, and denial of access to records within a system of records.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush is assigned a General Services Administration (GSA) security container in a vault where no guard is posted overnight. The material may go in only if an alarm is installed and personnel respond to it within 15 minutes. For which classification level is this added protection required?

answers.rationale: The container for this level needs continuous protection by guards or an alarm answered within 15 minutes.
Secret material must be stored in a container approved for its level, without the 15 minute alarm response stated.
Confidential material must be stored in a container approved for its level, without the 15 minute alarm response stated.
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) may be kept in unlocked desks after hours when building security is provided.

questions.stem: Before a deployment, one airman posts a photo of packed bags online, another mentions extra night shifts while chatting in a store line, and a third texts a friend that the gym schedule is canceled for months. No single detail names where or when the unit goes, but an adversary could combine them to work that out. Which Operations Security (OPSEC) term covers all three details?

answers.rationale: Critical information is what the adversary derives, the facts about friendly intentions such as where and when the unit goes.
Indicators are friendly detectable actions and open-source information that an adversary can piece together to derive critical information.
Open conversations fit the remark in the store line, but not the photo or the text message.
Private messaging fits the text to a friend, but not the photo or the remark in the store line.

questions.stem: MSgt Rush must pass a classified schedule change to another base within the hour. An ordinary office phone sits on the desk, but MSgt Rush walks to the vault and makes the call on a secure telephone instead. Which Communications Security (COMSEC) component is MSgt Rush applying by picking that system for the call?

answers.rationale: Cryptosecurity is the proper use of cryptographic systems to defeat cryptanalysis; the point here is choosing the system.
